Author: Rajesh Bindal
Bench: Rajesh Bindal

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil) No.2140/2024
 Avantika Ashok Sharma Petitione
 Versus
 Prateek Sharma Responde
 O R D E R
We have been informed by the learned counsel for the parties that the matter has been resolved between the parties by way of a settlement agreement dated 09.12.2024.

The parties have filed a joint application being IA No.301709/2024 seeking dissolution of marriage and a decree of divorce by mutual consent under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 between the parties.

As per the terms of the said Settlement Agreement, the monetary consideration of Rs.6,00,000/-
(Rupees Six Lacs only) by way of a demand draft bearing No.540844 dated 11.11.2024, drawn on State Bank of India, Branch Gandhidham has been handed over by the learned counsel for the respondent-husband to the counsel for the petitioner-wife towards the full and final settlement of all her claims towards alimony, maintenance (past, present and future), belongings and other claims.

It is agreed between the Reason: parties that after the filing of the application under Section 142 of the Constitution of India, 1950, the parties shall exchange the ornaments/articles as per the terms of the settlement deed.
Needful has been done.

In view of the settlement arrived at,
the proceedings in (i) and (ii) stand quashed.
The Original Petition (HM) No.1070 of 2022 pending before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Ghaziabad stands disposed of as having been settled.
We make it clear that the parties shall not pursue have any claims against each other in the future.
In view of the above, the IA No.301709/2024 stands allowed.
Accordingly, by invoking our power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, there shall be a mutual divorce between the parties, as agreed upon.

The Transfer Petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
